_comment: SHAPE EXAMPLE ONLY — do not publish verbatim. The ask-project skill tells the agent to INSPECT the real repo and TAILOR these to the actual project, dropping any the code or the user's instructions already answer. Ten generic-software questions spanning the coverage dimensions, each showing the full QuestionInput shape the contract expects. Publish with: node bin/ask.mjs ask --file <your-tailored-file>.json

questions.title: In one sentence, what is the single most important thing this project must do well?
questions.context: The whole build orients around this; everything else is secondary. Pinning it now prevents scope drift later.
questions.consequence: Determines which features are core vs nice-to-have, and what we optimize first.

questions.title: Who is the primary user we are building for first?
questions.context: Audience drives UX, defaults, and tone. Building for everyone usually means building for no one.
questions.consequence: Shapes onboarding, terminology, accessibility priorities, and which platform we target first.

options.label: A mix — specify in a follow-up

questions.title: What one measurable outcome tells us this is working in 90 days?
questions.context: A single success metric keeps the roadmap honest and lets us say no to distractions.
questions.consequence: Decides what we instrument, what the dashboard shows, and how we prioritize.

questions.title: Which capabilities are in scope for the FIRST usable release?
questions.context: Cutting v1 scope to the essential path ships value sooner and de-risks the rest.
questions.consequence: Everything unchecked moves to a later milestone; checked items become the build plan now.
questions.recommendation: Recommended: start with core CRUD + sign-in; defer payments and admin unless they are the point of the product.

questions.title: Where should the primary data live?
questions.context: The datastore is a near-irreversible choice; picking it early avoids a painful migration later.
questions.consequence: Determines the ORM, query patterns, hosting, backup story, and read/write scaling approach.
questions.recommendation: Recommended: D1/SQLite for an edge-first app; Postgres if you need complex relational queries from day one.

questions.title: How should users authenticate?
questions.context: Auth is deeply coupled to sessions and user data; changing providers later is weeks of work.
questions.consequence: Sets the sign-in UX, session model, and what identity data we store.

options.label: No auth yet — single-tenant for now

questions.recommendation: Recommended: a managed provider to avoid rolling our own credential storage.

questions.title: Where will this be deployed and run?
questions.context: The runtime target constrains the framework, cold-start budget, and ops model.
questions.consequence: Decides the build output, runtime APIs we can use, and the deploy pipeline.

questions.title: What are the performance expectations (e.g. page-load, API latency)?
questions.context: Explicit targets prevent both under-building and premature optimization.
questions.consequence: Guides caching, bundle budgets, and whether we need background jobs or streaming.

questions.title: If the product uses AI, what must it never do, and where must a human stay in control?
questions.context: Setting guardrails up front keeps AI features safe, on-brand, and trustworthy.
questions.consequence: Defines which actions are auto vs confirmed, what gets logged, and the fallback when the model is unsure.

questions.title: What is the testing bar before something ships to users?
questions.context: Agreeing the bar now avoids relitigating 'is this done?' on every change.
questions.consequence: Sets whether we gate on unit tests, end-to-end flows, and accessibility checks.

options.label: End-to-end on key flows + unit tests + a11y checks
Unit tests on core logic only

questions.recommendation: Recommended: end-to-end on the critical path plus units on core logic — the highest confidence per hour.
